confirmed: Source: arXiv:2502.14747v1 [cs.HC], 20 Feb 2025; the first-page footnote identifies a preprint accepted at CHI 2025. The local PDF has 28 pages; its title and five authors match the form (PDF p. 1). The complete markdown, including Appendices A-F, was read.

The summative sample contains 16 distinct professional designers, each completing both conditions; the two arm counts are repeated observations on the same people. Table 1 and the Figure 7/8 rating distributions support 16 analyzed, below 50; a randomized count and post-assignment exclusions are not stated (PDF p. 7, Table 1; p. 12, Sections 6 and 6.1.1; p. 13, Section 6.1.6; pp. 14-15, Figures 7-8).
Summative participants have 1-12 years of experience, M = 4.6, and 6 also participated in the formative study, as the form states (PDF p. 13, Section 6.1.6).

Each condition used a 30-minute task gathering at least three reference sets; the two topics were a Mayan Observatory and Planetarium and a Tibetan Meditation Research Center (PDF p. 12, Sections 6.1.1-6.1.2).
AIdeation uses GPT-4o-2024-05-13 for idea generation, GPT-4o Vision for image captions, DALL-E 3 for images, and Bing Image Search for references (PDF p. 11, Section 5.2.1).

Creativity preference: Mean = 5.56, p = 0.001, 81% preferring AIdeation, exactly as reported; this is a preference about creativity support, not an output creativity score (PDF p. 13, Section 7.1.2; p. 14, Figure 7a; p. 24, Appendix A, item 4).
Idea-quality preference: Mean = 4.31, p = 0.41, exactly as reported (PDF p. 14, Section 7.2; p. 15, Figure 8).

Efficiency in generating varied ideas: Mean = 5.44, p = 0.003, 75% preferring AIdeation, exactly as reported (PDF p. 14, Section 7.2; p. 15, Figure 8). Participants were asked to disregard image-generation time for efficiency questions (PDF p. 12, Section 6.1.4).

The questionnaire uses a 7-point preference scale, with 7 favoring AIdeation and 1 favoring the original workflow; the analysis is a one-sample Wilcoxon signed-rank test against neutral midpoint 4 (PDF pp. 12-13, Section 6.1.4).

All three listed outcomes correctly have scored_on_output = false and measure = self_report. External expert evaluation of summative outputs was explicitly not conducted; Appendix A asks which system supports creativity, quality, and efficiency (PDF p. 13, Section 6.1.5; p. 24, Appendix A, items 4, 9-10).

The one-line finding correctly reproduces the 16-person comparison, creativity mean/p-value, and idea-quality mean/p-value as self-reported preferences (PDF p. 13, Sections 6.1.6 and 7.1.2; p. 14, Section 7.2).

The field study involves 8 of the summative designers in 4 studios for one week; creativity/quality feedback is qualitative and participant-reported, including reports of director/client reactions (PDF p. 16, Sections 8-8.2; p. 17, Section 8.3.1; p. 20, Section 9.4.1).

Core = no and context_class = none remain appropriate: the sample is below 50, randomized condition order is not established, and no qualifying scored creativity/diversity comparison is reported. The formative interviews and field deployment do not supply such a randomized study (PDF p. 6, Sections 4.1-4.3; pp. 12-13, Sections 6.1.1 and 6.1.5-6.1.6; pp. 16-17, Section 8; p. 20, Section 9.4.1).
This is an empirical system paper, not a synthesis; there are no pooled effect estimates or standardization intervals to extract (PDF p. 2, Introduction; Sections 4, 6, and 8).
summary: The 16-person comparison uses self-reported preferences and does not establish randomized assignment, so the core exclusion remains supported. All three reported results and the source version are accurate, but six corrections are needed for design coding, baseline AI availability, omitted studies, appendices, and company involvement.
